title: Which GLP-1s reduce inflammation?
summary: Semaglutide, tirzepatide, liraglutide, and retatrutide lower CRP in trials. Here are the numbers, their limits, and how statins compare.
body_markdown:
Several GLP-1-based treatments lower inflammation markers as well as weight and blood sugar. **Semaglutide, tirzepatide, liraglutide, and retatrutide all have randomized trial evidence of lower C-reactive protein (CRP).** Tirzepatide also activates the GIP receptor, and investigational retatrutide activates GIP and glucagon receptors in addition to GLP-1. Some studies show reductions in inflammatory signals such as interleukin-6 (IL-6). The evidence does not establish which drug is best for treating inflammation itself.


[hs-CRP](https://www.empirical.health/tests/hs-crp/) is a high-sensitivity test for CRP, a protein your liver makes in response to inflammation. It measures the low concentrations used to assess cardiovascular risk.


## Which GLP-1s lower CRP, and by how much?


Medication What studies found Study context


**Semaglutide** (Wegovy, Ozempic) **39–48% lower CRP versus placebo** at 68 weeks Weekly 2.4 mg in adults with overweight or obesity, with or without diabetes;[STEP 1–3 analysis](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36467859/)


**Tirzepatide** (Zepbound, Mounjaro), a dual GIP/GLP-1 agonist **51–65% lower hs-CRP from baseline** , versus 22% with placebo, at 72 weeks Weekly 5–15 mg in a roughly 400-person subset of adults with overweight or obesity without diabetes;[SURMOUNT-1 analysis](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jacc.2026.04.044)


**Liraglutide** (Saxenda, Victoza) **38% lower hs-CRP from baseline** , versus 10% with placebo, at 56 weeks Daily 3 mg in adults with overweight or obesity without diabetes;[FDA review of SCALE](https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2014/206321Orig1s000MedR.pdf)


**Retatrutide** , an investigational triple GLP-1/GIP/glucagon agonist **62.6% lower hs-CRP from baseline** at 12 mg, versus 24.9% with placebo, at 80 weeks Weekly 12 mg in adults with obesity or overweight without diabetes;[TRIUMPH-1 trial](https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa2604169) ,[trial results table](https://www.lilly.com/hcp/medical-information/answers/what-are-the-results-of-retatrutide-from-triumph-1-in-participants-with-obesity-or-overweight-without-type-2-diabetes-386151)


*The bars show separate trials with different comparison bases, so their lengths do not rank drug potency.[STEP 1–3](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36467859/) ,[SURMOUNT-1](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jacc.2026.04.044) ,[SCALE](https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2014/206321Orig1s000MedR.pdf) ,[TRIUMPH-1](https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa2604169) .*


These aren’t head-to-head comparisons. The studies used different populations, doses, durations, and analyses. **The semaglutide row reports an effect relative to placebo; the other rows report changes from baseline in each arm.** For example, the 62.6% hs-CRP decrease with retatrutide includes change also seen in its placebo group. Subtracting the two percentages gives 37.7 percentage points, but that arithmetic is not necessarily the trial’s modeled placebo-adjusted treatment effect. The percentages describe the studied doses, not every formulation sold under each brand. Most inflammation results were secondary or exploratory analyses.


## What about inflammation markers besides hs-CRP?


In the same[SURMOUNT-1 analysis](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jacc.2026.04.044) , tirzepatide lowered **IL-6** , an inflammatory signaling protein, versus placebo. White blood cell counts also fell significantly versus placebo at the 10 mg and 15 mg doses.


There are signals for other drugs, too. A small[study of dulaglutide and liraglutide](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34518091/) reported lower IL-6 after treatment. That study lacked a placebo group, so it provides weaker evidence of a drug effect than a randomized placebo-controlled trial.


## Is it just the weight loss?


Weight loss explains at least part of the improvement. In STEP, CRP reductions tracked with weight loss; in SURMOUNT-1, mediation analyses suggested weight loss accounted for much of the longer-term reduction in hs-CRP and IL-6. Those analyses can’t definitively separate weight loss from direct drug effects.


A lower hs-CRP shows less systemic inflammation, but it doesn’t prove that lowering CRP caused a health benefit or that a medication treats every inflammatory condition. Drug choice should follow evidence for your condition and overall health. If you’re tracking hs-CRP, interpret repeat measurements with your clinician: an infection can temporarily raise it, obscuring the longer-term trend.


## How do statins compare?


Statins lower hs-CRP too: in the randomized[JUPITER trial](https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa0807646) , rosuvastatin 20 mg lowered median hs-CRP by 37% and LDL cholesterol by 50%, alongside fewer cardiovascular events. Because both markers fell, the trial cannot isolate which change drove the benefit, and its different population makes the 37% result unsuitable for ranking rosuvastatin against these GLP-1-based treatments.
